files: Legal documents: contracts, filings, case documents, and statutory text.
value: Legal-domain AI built for law firms rather than adapted from a general assistant. Handles legal research, document drafting, contract review, and due diligence in the contexts a lawyer actually works in, not the contexts a general AI was trained on.
engine: Built on frontier models (primarily OpenAI and Anthropic) with legal-domain fine-tuning and retrieval.
latency: Fast enough for interactive research. Document review at scale is batch.

pricing.includes: Data controls, professional liability alignment, admin oversight

quality: Strongest for legal English and legal reasoning. Outputs still require lawyer review before any client-facing use.
tagline: AI for legal work, built specifically for law firms and legal departments.
use_cases: Legal research and issue spotting across case law and statutes
Due diligence document review at scale
integrations: Document management systems used in legal practice
governance_note: The legal professional responsibility question is the same regardless of tool: a lawyer cannot delegate judgment to an AI, and outputs must be reviewed before they touch client work. What changes is which tasks can be accelerated. The professional liability point is that if Harvey produces a flawed contract clause and a lawyer submits it without review, the lawyer's error, not the vendor's. On the data side, privilege must be maintained for client matter inputs, which requires a confirmed data path under the firm's privilege policy, not just the vendor's standard terms.
training_optout: Legal-grade data terms. Client matter data is not used to train models. Verify the DPA for your jurisdiction.
